title: NHLBI counts three non-REM stages, and OpenStax Psychology counts four
summary: NHLBI describes three non-REM stages plus REM. The first edition of OpenStax Psychology describes four non-REM stages and then REM as a fifth stage.
body: Read side by side, the two opened texts do not use the same stage count. NHLBI's stages page says non-REM sleep has three stages, then describes REM separately. The first edition of OpenStax Psychology, in its stages section, says sleep divides into REM and non-REM, and that the first four stages are non-REM while the fifth is REM. Both texts tie ordinary dreaming to the REM phase. The card records the difference in how the pages divide the night. It does not decide which count a sleep lab should use. The OpenStax sentence is paraphrased from the first edition, which is CC BY 4.0. Evidence stays at moderate because that host's ceiling is moderate.
